mechanics.entry_paths:
The three code references to 0x005b2490 are not call sites; each is the JMP of a two-instruction adjustor, read as bytes:
  0x0057a5d0  83 E9 04      SUB ECX,0x4     ; E9 B8 7E 03 00  JMP 0x005b2490
  0x0057a5f0  83 E9 10      SUB ECX,0x10    ; E9 98 7E 03 00  JMP 0x005b2490
  0x005b8550  83 E9 14      SUB ECX,0x14    ; E9 38 9F FF FF  JMP 0x005b2490
This is the corroboration abi_derived.conventions.corroboration ('not_available') was missing. A first argument that a stub reduces by a constant before the transfer, and which is then never consumed, is a `this` pointer; a cdecl parameter is passed by value and is not adjusted. Each adjustor is itself referenced only from data, so there is no direct caller of this body anywhere in the image: all eighteen xrefs are either data references into slot tables or one of these three JMPs. That is a statement about static entry paths, not a claim that nothing calls it -- an indirect call through a table slot has no static edge.
mechanics.slot_occupancy:
The body's own address is a slot occupant in the tables below, read by dumping the tables' bytes rather than inferred:
  0x013f57f8  slot +0x00 = 0x005b2490. The two dwords below the table head are 0x008816f0 and 0x00000000, the shape of a complete-object locator and a null destructor entry, so 0x013f57f8 is a table head and not an interior slot.
  0x013f7028  slot +0x10 = 0x005b2490, with slot +0x04 = 0x005b8550 (the -0x14 adjustor) one slot above it.
The record associates 12 tables with this VA and the xref export carries 15 data references to it, 14 of which are the three adjustors' own slots. Nothing is named for any of those slots: this binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so the record has no slot name and none is invented. In particular the two tables do not license a claim that the slot means the same thing in both, and no member is modelled at the receiver's +0x00 -- the body never reads it.
mechanics.return_semantics_machine: EAX carries the value, and the returned word is the SAME word that was stored, which is a fact rather than a reading: 0x005b2490 loads the dword into EAX, 0x005b2493 increments all 32 bits of EAX, and 0x005b2494 stores EAX itself. The width is 32 bits -- a dword is read, all of EAX is incremented, a dword is stored. Wraparound is the machine's: 0xffffffff increments to 0x00000000 and 0x7fffffff to 0x80000000. The SIGN is not fixed: INC EAX is bit-identical for signed and unsigned, nothing in the body tests bit 31, and the record's own return_semantics is 'unclassified_in_EAX' with RT2 register_class 'aggregate_unknown'.
mechanics.receiver_writes: Exactly one, and it is a dword: 0x005b2494 writes the four bytes at receiver+0x18..+0x1b. Nothing else in the receiver is written, nothing at +0x00..+0x17 or +0x1c upward is touched, and abi_derived.receiver.written_through is 1. The write is a read-modify-write of the same dword the first instruction read, so the word's new value is the old value plus one, computed in EAX.

return_semantics.value: the receiver's dword at +0x18, after being incremented by one with 32-bit wraparound. EAX at the RET holds exactly the dword that 0x005b2494 wrote.
return_semantics.ownership: Not applicable and not claimed. The body acquires and releases nothing, holds no pointer, and performs no lifetime work of any kind; the only memory it touches is the receiver's own dword, in place.
return_semantics.lifetime: The value is a copy of a word, not a reference: it is returned by value in a register, so nothing the caller receives is tied to the receiver's storage. The single mutation it performs is permanent, not scoped -- the dword at +0x18 is left incremented, and the body has no path on which it restores it.

unresolved_questions: What is the word at receiver+0x18? Nothing in this body or in any record consulted here says: it is read, incremented and written, and nothing tests or constrains its value, so it could be a counter, a version, a sequence number, a reference count, an index or a handle. Naming it would be a member story four instructions cannot carry, so the package names it a word and leaves the question here.

Is the word signed or unsigned? INC EAX is bit-identical for signed and unsigned, nothing in the body tests bit 31, and abi_derived's return_semantics is 'unclassified_in_EAX' (RT2 register_class aggregate_unknown). The reconstruction models it as an unsigned 32-bit word -- which is what fixes the 0xffffffff -> 0x00000000 wrap the machine performs -- and the SIGN itself is unresolved. The declared return type is now spelled std::uint32_t rather than the `Word` alias, and that spelling fixes the WIDTH and the wrap only: unsigned is what the wraparound test at 0xffffffff needs to be defined, and it is not a claim that the original's type is unsigned, because INC EAX cannot distinguish the two and no instruction here reads bit 31. Whether the true type is signed changes no observable behaviour of THIS body and changes the meaning of its return value at every caller.

What are the eleven other vtables this address is associated with, and does the slot mean the same thing in all of them? The record associates 12 tables, the xref export carries 15 data references, and this binary has no MSVC RTTI, so no slot name is recoverable from it. The two displacements this package verified (+0x00 of the table at 0x013f57f8 and +0x10 of the table at 0x013f7028) are the only slot facts claimed, and the fact that the same address sits at two different displacements in two tables is itself unexplained.

Is the receiver the head of its object or a sub-object? The body never stores ECX, so a this-adjusting caller is invisible from inside it. The three adjustors (-0x04, -0x10, -0x14) prove the word lives at more than one displacement within a hierarchy, but which class each table belongs to is not established by anything in this package.

What is the true size of the receiver? 0x1c is a lower bound this body proves (0x18 + 4) and nothing more. The object is certainly larger -- it is polymorphic, so a dispatch word exists at +0x00 -- but this body never reads or writes any byte outside 0x18..0x1b and no consulted record sizes it.

Does any caller use the returned value, and as what? The body is entered only through a table slot, so its callers are the dispatch sites, which this package did not enumerate. The return is the incremented word; whether a caller treats it as a count, an index, a new generation or an opaque handle is not established here.
